title: Dialogue management panel for critical NPC conversations
summary: A GM-facing info panel for running important NPC conversations: player goals, NPC goals, hard lines the NPC won't cross, what's coercible, and a subject list each with a DC and one-click buttons to record degree of success as the scene plays out.
description:
Stated directly: 'We build a dialogue managing system which allows the group to have critical conversations with NPCs.' The panel should make it easy for the GM to manage the conversation live: player goals, the NPC's own goals, hard lines the NPC won't cross, information about what could plausibly be coerced from them, and — the mechanical core — a long list of subjects each with an associated DC, plus buttons to record the degree of success (critical failure / failure / neutral / success / critical success) as the players attempt them.

Structurally this is the same shape challenge.schema.json already models (a set of DC'd checks with per-degree outcomes), wearing a live-session UI. Feeds directly into chat-log-knowledge-base (recorded outcomes need to be durably queryable after the session, not just visible in the moment) and is probably a component of campaign-managing-system rather than a fully standalone tool.

REVISITED 2026-09-06 (design/npc-social-intel.md). Two things. First, a small correction worth recording rather than silently fixing: SF2E's real degree of success is FOUR tiers (critical failure / failure / success / critical success), never five — this entry's own 'neutral' has no RAW equivalent as a check outcome. Checked against real Diplomacy/Intimidation actions: a plain Failure on Make an Impression or Request already has no listed effect, which is what reads as 'neutral' in play — that's the genuine four-tier structure, not an invented fifth rung. Second, this panel now has a standing companion rather than starting cold each time: the Character Card gives every recurring NPC a persistent, hand-authored Facts list (revealed permanently through play) and a real Attitude state (SF2E's own Hostile/Unfriendly/Indifferent/Friendly/Helpful scale) that carries between scenes — this panel is the live tool you open into that standing state, not a separate live-only system.
sourceContext: User planning message on dialogue/journal/campaign-management systems, prior to the ideas/ system existing — originally captured as prose in design/campaign-arc.md's 'Foundry module: new concept threads' section, migrated here on audit.
